behavior: Terrestrial and often inconspicuous; forages on the ground for small insects and other invertebrates, adding seeds and berries especially in winter. When flushed, it rises in a slightly bounding flight that can reveal the white sides of the tail. It also uses low elevated perches and performs a short, repetitive song flight.
field_marks: Small, slender pipit with a relatively long tail
Dark eye with a narrow pale eye-ring and weak pale eyebrow
Olive-brown upperparts with dark streaking and pale-edged wing feathers
Buff-white underparts with bold dark streaks across the breast and flanks
Pale pinkish legs; brown tail with narrow white outer edges
habitat: Open ground with low vegetation, including grassland, pasture, heath, moorland, bogs, and lightly farmed fields; also salt marsh and occasionally open woodland in winter.
